::: {.why}
The asymmetry you measured last night has two competing explanations that are still argued about, and it is the reason an equity index option surface is skewed rather than smiling.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Report the size of the leverage effect in your data, as the difference in next-day volatility after down days versus up days of equal magnitude.
- State the two standard explanations and name an observation that would distinguish them.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Measure it properly: regress next-day absolute return on today's signed return and on today's absolute return jointly. The coefficient on the signed term is the effect. Report it with a standard error, and match up-days against down-days of comparable magnitude so the result is not just a size effect.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Test it across assets: run the same regression on a currency pair and on a commodity ETF. The effect is an equity phenomenon more than a universal one, and finding out where it is absent is more informative than confirming it where it is present.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Write two sentences on the competing explanations, the mechanical leverage story and the volatility feedback story, and one line on what observation would separate them.
:::
:::
